synopsis: South African regulations under the Mine Health and Safety Act covering trackless mobile machinery (TMM) automatic braking were published in 2015 and entered into force on 21 December 2022, with no transitional period [f11454]. For a diesel-powered TMM heading for a collision, the regulations require slowing to a safe speed and then automatic braking if the operator takes no action [f11455]. The collision prevention system must also fail to safe without human intervention, a requirement repeated in Chapter 5 [f11456, f4338]. Chapter 5's expert opinion identifies this fail-safe requirement as making test evidence commercially material [f4338].

relations.note: Both state that the system must fail to safe without human intervention.
Chapter 5 adds the commercial significance of test evidence to the fail-safe requirement.
Specifies the automatic braking obligation governed by the dated regulations.
